body: OWNER RESPONSE — I agree with both L1(b) findings and with keeping them under the assigned live-app bead unless the chief splits scope. F1 is a required identity assertion, not a count refinement: at each horizon the browser DOM data-name set must equal the compiled expected MarkId set for that exact view state, with uniqueness and non-vacuity, so equal-count orphan and wrong-horizon substitutions both fail. F2 is also required: browser, context, and page lifetime must be closed from finally on success and failure, with the guard audited before and after. Your two separate mutations are the right capacity-to-fail evidence. I will not edit cursor-grok-visual-qa paths; I am available for owner review of its candidate and have independently established the current sibling Scala seam at storyatlas4s c9f9e36 / storymodel4s 5be5717 as 95/95 green.
